rubric_definition: After you make the edit that one reviewer is asking for, does the other reviewer's comment still stand? If it is discharged too, the two findings are one defect; if it survives, they are different defects that share a location. If a reviewer offers two alternative fixes, either one discharging the other comment makes it one defect. Contradictory prescriptions to the same lines are different defects, because no single edit satisfies both.
evidence: Finding A concerns an undocumented plugin-ordering invariant in packages/notes/src/view/preview.ts; Finding B asks for language tags on fenced code blocks in docs markdown files. Adding a fence info string does nothing for the ordering comment, and vice versa.

panel.finding_key: packages/notes/src/view/preview.ts::new undocumented plugin-ordering invariant: any plugin registered after `listemptybulletplugin` that replaces `list`/`lheading` silently discards this fix, and any plugin added before it gets its `list` wrapper permanently baked in
panel.summary: New undocumented plugin-ordering invariant: any plugin registered after `listEmptyBulletPlugin` that replaces `list`/`lheading` silently discards this fix, and any plugin added before it gets its `list` wrapper permanently baked in
panel.evidence: `getRuleFn` snapshots the `list` rule at install time and `md.block.ruler.at('lheading', ...)` overwrites whatever is registered. Today `md.use(taskLists)` (preview.ts:36), `md.use(katexPlugin)` (preview.ts:39) and `md.use(detailsPlugin)` (preview.ts:44) all run first and none replace `list`/`lheading`, so the current chain is fine — but the ordering requirement exists only implicitly. `packages/notes/src/view/details-plugin.ts:104-106` registers `details` with `alt: ['paragraph','reference','blockquote','list']`, showing plugins here do touch the same ruler surfaces. A comment at preview.ts:46-48 stating 'must stay last / after any plugin touching list or lheading' would preserve the invariant.
